capabilities.notes: ReadOS owns a narrow, backend-only virtual POSIX pwd/echo/cat/ls/du/find slice plus safe virtual-workspace subsets of printf/head/tail/wc and a bounded literal-byte grep. Find is metadata-only with virtual start paths, -name/-iname glob predicates, -type f/d predicates, deterministic traversal, .msp exclusion, and bounded depth/entries/pattern/scan/output/cancellation policies; it never follows symlink/reparse/special entries. All commands use bounded binary output, explicit stdin, validated virtual paths, deterministic registry composition, 32 KiB-or-backend range reads where applicable, and aggregate scan/recursion/entry policies. Grep supports only -n, -i, -v, -c, -l, -q, and one -r with linear-time literal matching; .msp components are excluded. It is an authored adaptation informed by public MSP descriptions, not raw MSP source or full command parity; broader native/msp-core command inventory and upstream parity are not evidence for this pack.

ReadOS owns a neutral, host-free WorkspaceBackend contract with bounded in-memory WorkspaceFS behavior, including virtual WorkspaceRead and WorkspaceWrite. Process, PTY, event-streaming, and cancellation capabilities remain explicit unsupported contract states; this local virtual slice is distinct from Windows host-backed capability status and does not establish upstream MSP parity.

The modular Windows adapter now binds a fixed local NTFS root and uses open-first final-handle containment for bounded stat/list/range-read and whole-file replace-or-create writes. Focused Windows tests cover binary data, deterministic listing, hidden paths, ADS/device/UNC syntax, outward reparse escape, bounds, and path-free diagnostics. The public API contains no legacy types. Process and PTY remain Unsupported; common cross-platform fixtures, product policy/write-trash integration, and full upstream parity are not claimed.

Migration oracle only: this explicit-feature bridge exposes bridge-owned /workspace DTOs over the excluded legacy retained-root implementation. The supported H3.1 implementation is now native/msp-backend-windows; this bridge has no mutable or process surface and must not receive new product features.

ReadOS owns a narrow Linux host workspace adapter. It binds a trusted root only in the platform constructor, probes openat2, then resolves below an owned root descriptor with RESOLVE_BENEATH, RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS, and RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS. It exposes /workspace rather than virtual root, rejects symlinks, special files, hidden .msp, traversal, and host syntax, redacts host errors, and reports process/PTY unsupported. Bounded file/directory rename uses descriptor-relative renameat2 and bounded file/empty-directory delete uses unlinkat; recursive delete, trash, directory creation, and unsafe fallback remain unsupported. Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS container image sha256:33ceb71981b602c1a7443a53469e4dba065f7503eab3078a2d7a57a2ab987517 passes the focused 9-test suite, workspace tests, Linux target check, Clippy, and package-content checks; the hosted ubuntu-latest workflow remains the reproducible CI gate but is not claimed as run here. This does not establish upstream MSP parity.

ReadOS's non-executing CommandPlanner enforces bounded input, parses supported simple commands, and expands only caller-supplied context into a sanitized plan. It does not resolve PATH, inspect a filesystem or environment, or execute; the local planner slice does not establish upstream shell or command parity.

ReadOS owns a stateless virtual command runtime that connects the caller-owned planner to the registered virtual command pack and neutral backend. It preserves bounded binary results and leaves policy, approval, terminal routing, and product audit above the boundary; it performs no process or host-environment work and does not claim full upstream runtime parity.

ReadOS owns a separate Windows-local release-verified 13-export C ABI over the deterministic virtual command runtime. The release script checks the PE export count and runs the C11 header plus C++ consumer smokes; the managed adapter is separately focused below. Linux and Android release artifacts are not claimed by this Windows evidence. It is not the legacy msp-ffi ABI or the managed reados-msp-native/1 transport.

Focused managed contract tests always run. The single real-DLL fact is explicitly skipped when READOS_MSP_COMMAND_RUNTIME_FFI_DLL is absent or not Windows; setting that variable to a fully qualified release DLL enables it. The adapter is opt-in and does not alter product routing.

The reviewed Windows checkout does not claim a Linux target build or runtime execution. Android is tracked separately by command-runtime-ffi-android-aar; no Linux or non-arm64 Android availability is inferred from that compile/package evidence. The top-level upstream status remains blocked.

The Ubuntu portable-rust-ci Android job installs the pinned NDK/CMake toolchain, builds the real Rust cdylib, runs Kotlin/JNI compile and unit smoke tests, verifies all 13 Rust symbols, and checks the release AAR contains both arm64-v8a shared objects and Kotlin classes. Local API 35 x86_64 emulator evidence now also passes the real androidTest suite, including the SAF/ContentResolver projected-workspace tests; the test-only x86_64 artifact does not widen the published arm64-v8a AAR. Arm64 device execution, SAF write-back, and product routing remain separate H3.3/H5 work. Windows/legacy ABI remains unchanged.

ReadOS owns a host-neutral H4.1 registration and launch-plan contract. It combines verified platform-neutral bundle evidence with explicit profiles, bundle-relative executable digests, virtual workspace mode, bounded argv/environment/output/time/memory/process/file limits, mandatory cancellation and process-tree cleanup, and license/NOTICE provenance. It rejects PATH/loader keys, shell wrappers, host paths, and arbitrary shell fields; launch-time bundle and executable identity revalidation is pure and path-free. The 13-test focused suite passed on 2026-08-26. No process provider is claimed; H4.2 owns real Windows/non-Windows launch evidence.

ReadOS owns the platform process lifecycle below the host-neutral provider contract. It accepts only a host-bound executable already resolved and digest-verified by the Host/provider, maps virtual /workspace cwd below a trusted root, clears inherited environment, bounds stdout/stderr and wall time, redacts bound host paths, and kills the child tree through a Windows Job Object or Unix process group. The focused Windows and local WSL Linux tests passed 6 backend tests each on 2026-08-26, including cancellation, timeout, complete virtual-namespace validation, and repository symlink/junction escape tests. This is not a general shell/PTY backend and does not own policy, approval, audit, or provider selection.

The H4.2 provider is a fixed, read-only Git profile catalog: status, files, head, and bounded log. It supplies isolated Git configuration, disables hooks, prompts, credential helpers, optional locks, and network protocols, and delegates process/cwd confinement to msp-process-backend. Five provider tests passed on both Windows and local WSL Linux on 2026-08-26. Windows evidence used Git 2.54.0.windows.1 at C:/Program Files/Git/cmd/git.exe (SHA-256 81ef35ae005ca9318018d18e3327578ce939fb99feaad6b2d7c8ab15f3de8db5); local WSL Linux evidence used Git 2.55.0 at /usr/bin/git (SHA-256 93473c28694fd72bd889364107cd2770514de59780885a6a4aafca4d602e30ad). The crate contains provider manifests/provenance but does not redistribute either Git executable; no product routing or Android/Termux support is claimed.

H4.3 selects app-owned Toybox as the first Android provider direction, with fixed pwd/cat/ls profiles over an app-private projected workspace. The Kotlin provider is argv-only, digest-bound, environment-cleared, bounded, cancellable, and path-redacting; TermuxOptional fails closed. The app-owned binding now verifies fixed AAR metadata/assets, app-private workspace confinement, and the expected executable digest, while the Host catalog exposes only verified fixed profile launch plans. Hosting and Android focused tests passed; the x86_64 Android instrumentation APK and AAR gates passed against the real Rust artifact, and all 7 connected instrumentation tests passed on reados-api35-x86_64(AVD) - 15. /system/bin/toybox remains an oracle only; no Toybox executable is redistributed. Arm64 execution, reviewed binary packaging, Android Host policy/approval/audit routing, and product adoption remain open.
